storylines.label: Web Search
storylines.latest_title: I benchmarked 4 web search APIs for AI agents on 30 live queries

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek priced web search for agents at /bin/bash.75 per 1,000 calls on Oct 17, making search a metered line item. A long-horizon eval paper followed on Oct 26.
editorial.whats_new: A GitHub benchmark compares 4 web search APIs for AI agents on 30 live queries, the first head-to-head comparison in this thread.
editorial.why_it_matters: Search API choice now affects agent cost and answer quality, and neither the price point nor the benchmark is independently verified yet.
editorial.take_for_builders: Run your own production queries against your current search API and one alternative, tracking cost per 1,000 calls and answer quality before switching.

status.detail: Pricing, an evaluation framework and a hands-on API benchmark have appeared, but the sources are thin and unconfirmed.

storylines.label: Kimi K3.1
storylines.latest_title: Moonshot apologises after botched Kimi K3.1 Pro launch, restores user quotas

editorial.tldr: On Oct 16, coverage framed Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 as a name without a released model, and one report said a new Chinese export-license requirement for large AI models could affect it. On Oct 23, reports said it was being readied for release after Arena testing.
editorial.whats_new: On Oct 27, SCMP reported Moonshot apologised for the botched Kimi K3.1 Pro launch and restored user quotas, after the Oct 26 reset following complaints.
editorial.why_it_matters: Two quota interventions in two days show Pro-tier usage limits were unstable at launch, which affects capacity planning and reliability for anything routed to it.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your own evals on Kimi K3.1 Pro before routing traffic, and keep a fallback model until Moonshot publishes stable quota limits and license terms.

status.detail: Moonshot apologised for the launch and restored user quotas; a stable quota policy has not been reported.

storylines.label: Large Language
storylines.latest_title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models

editorial.tldr: This page groups items by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. Oct 9-22 items cover knowledge graphs, sycophancy, code-translation hallucinations, search agents, and spectral edits.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 26 adds a long-horizon web-search benchmark with failure-node localization, a neuron-steering method, self-evolving KG reasoning, and Reva, a real-time vulnerability detector for generated code.
editorial.why_it_matters: Treat this as a reading list, not a thread. For platform engineers the useful items are LongSearchEval (agent failure localization) and Reva (screening agent-written code), plus the code-translation hallucination catalog.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run coding agents, read Reva and check whether per-function vulnerability screening could sit before review; if you run search agents, try LongSearchEval's failure-node localization on your traces. Skip the rest unless it matches your domain.

storylines.label: Diffusion Language
storylines.latest_title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models

editorial.tldr: Diffusion language models first appeared here as the backbone of a tool-using chemistry agent. Days later they turned up on the offensive side, as a way to craft fluent black-box attacks on LLMs.
editorial.whats_new: A new paper distills a decoding schedule so diffusion LLMs commit tokens in fewer rounds, targeting the parallel-generation speedup that has been hard to realize.
editorial.why_it_matters: Diffusion LLMs only pay off for serving if parallel decoding cuts rounds without hurting quality; this is research-stage evidence, not a deployable runtime.
editorial.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet; if you prototype one, measure decoding rounds and quality against your autoregressive baseline, and include fluent-prompt attacks in red-team evals.

status.detail: Three arXiv papers, no production release: agents, attacks and decoding speed are each explored once.

storylines.label: Benchmarking Long-Horizon
storylines.latest_title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents

editorial.tldr: Doc2Harness opened the thread on Oct 14 by measuring how much the harness around a model, not just the model, drives long-horizon coding-agent results. Over the next week, papers added search-state learning (ClueFlow), error-recovery tests for computer-use agents (CUA-Recovery) and a continual-learning exam.
editorial.whats_new: FOCUS (Oct 26) proposes active critic learning to fix credit assignment under sparse outcome rewards, moving the thread from measuring long-horizon agents to training them.
editorial.why_it_matters: Long-horizon agent failures come from harness design, silent state corruption and weak credit assignment, so benchmarks that isolate those factors are more useful for platform decisions than single-score leaderboards.
editorial.take_for_builders: When evaluating a long-horizon agent, rerun it under your own harness and add an injected-error recovery case before trusting a leaderboard score.

status.detail: Five arXiv preprints, no independent replication yet; benchmarks and training methods are arriving together.

storylines.label: Inference Fast
storylines.latest_title: Show HN: Resin, fast native scheduler for LLM inference engines

editorial.tldr: Prime Intellect launched Prime Inference on Oct 8 as a hosted serving option for frontier open models. On Oct 21 the vLLM blog introduced Humming, a quantized-inference kernel library from Ant Group and the vLLM community.
editorial.whats_new: Resin, a native scheduler for LLM inference engines, appeared as a Show HN on Oct 26, extending the speed push from hosted serving and kernels to scheduling.
editorial.why_it_matters: Inference speed work is now landing at three layers (hosted serving, kernels, scheduling), so latency gains can come from swapping a layer instead of changing models.
editorial.take_for_builders: Benchmark Humming on your own quantized models and GPUs before adopting it, and treat Resin as an experiment until it publishes comparisons.

storylines.label: Auditing Evaluation
storylines.latest_title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing

editorial.tldr: Three papers in six days audit the measurements behind agent and model evaluation rather than the models. First came trace-derived labels, then a headline memory gain in XLand-MiniGrid.
editorial.whats_new: A new paper tests model self-confidence and LLM-as-a-judge as cheaper ways to audit human-in-the-loop evaluation, aiming for statistically sound accuracy estimates.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent eval scores are only as good as the labels and noise floors behind them; if parsers, detectors, seeds or judges are unreliable, regressions and gains in your CI evals can be artifacts.
editorial.take_for_builders: Audit your own eval harness: spot-check detector labels against raw traces, rerun headline gains across seeds and maps, and calibrate any LLM judge against a human-labeled sample before trusting it.

storylines.label: Reinforcement Learning
storylines.latest_title: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors

editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 26: three arXiv papers turn RL on agent failures: MiRL targets terminal-agent misbehaviors, CalibraRL targets RAG hallucinations, and a video-editing study shows fine-grained credit can hurt.
editorial.why_it_matters: The newest papers frame RL as a reliability tool: train against named failures (MiRL), reward calibrated abstention (CalibraRL), and test whether per-step credit helps (it can hurt). All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, log recurring failure modes and test error-targeted RL (MiRL) against them, and A/B fine-grained credit assignment against episode-level reward before adopting it; treat paper results as unreplicated until you rerun them on your own evals.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest aim RL at agent reliability and credit-assignment limits.

storylines.label: On-Policy Distillation
storylines.latest_title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation

editorial.tldr: Papers from Oct 14 onward apply on-policy distillation (training a student on its own sampled trajectories, scored by a teacher) to translation, long-horizon coding agents, and the question of when the student should follow the teacher.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 26: EvoRouter, an arXiv paper, uses insight-guided on-policy distillation to pick models, agent counts and skills for multi-agent web-query serving at lower cost.
editorial.why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is moving from model post-training into serving decisions such as multi-agent routing, so cost-focused teams can test it on configuration choices, not only on small models.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you distill small models or tune multi-agent configs, run an on-policy versus SFT comparison on your own trajectories and query mix before adopting either; none of these papers has independent replication yet.

storylines.label: DeepSeek Flash
storylines.latest_title: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash first showed up in deployments: Dolphin's inference API went live Oct 11 and AMD MI355X posted AA-AgentPerf results Oct 14. Two OrcaRouter comparisons on Oct 16 then priced it against Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Step 5 Preview.
editorial.whats_new: A third-party paper (Oct 26) evaluates DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss-of-control and harmful-manipulation risks, adding independent safety evidence to a release that so far had only performance and price coverage.
editorial.why_it_matters: Flash-1017 is cheaper and stronger on agentic tasks, and an independent safety evaluation now exists. Teams giving it autonomy or tool access can weigh its findings alongside cost-per-task numbers.
editorial.take_for_builders: Rerun your agent eval and cost-per-task numbers on Flash-1017 before switching, read the Oct 26 risk evaluation before granting it autonomy or tool access, and test the search API against your current tool.

status.detail: Flash-1017 is out; an independent risk evaluation was published Oct 26.

storylines.label: Learning Through
storylines.latest_title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing

editorial.tldr: A run of arXiv papers on how agents learn from their own trajectories. ClueFlow credits search steps by research-state transitions, and a memory-skill paper tackles lifelong learning under a bounded context window.
editorial.whats_new: A multimodal RL paper on video editing asks when fine-grained credit assignment helps agent training and when it fails to improve task performance.
editorial.why_it_matters: Credit assignment and memory design determine how agents improve from experience, which affects how you build training signals and context management for long-horizon agents.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adding per-step rewards to an agent RL setup, run an ablation against outcome-only rewards on your own tasks.

storylines.label: DeepSeek DeepInfer
storylines.latest_title: LongSearchEval: Evaluating Long-Horizon Web Search Capabilities of Large Language Models via a Trajectory-Aware Agent Framework with Failure-Node Localization

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek said on Oct 20 it is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the software that serves its production models. Coverage first framed it as a way to cut AI operating costs, then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic.
editorial.whats_new: No new DeepInfer coverage since Oct 21; Oct 22-26 items (agent evals, multi-agent and web-search papers) are unrelated and the efficiency claims remain unreproduced.
editorial.why_it_matters: A production-proven open inference stack gives platform teams a reference for serving cost and throughput that vLLM-style deployments can be benchmarked against.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo and license before changing a serving stack; treat the margin figures as unverified until someone reproduces them on non-DeepSeek hardware.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; independent reproduction of the efficiency claims has not appeared yet.
